english.title: Fail to store fuel oil on a farm as required by regulations
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) had custody or control of fuel oil on a farm, namely **(..SPECIFY THE FARM AND LOCATION..), which was stored otherwise than in accordance with regulation 5 of the Control of Pollution (Silage, Slurry and Agricultural Fuel Oil) Regulations 1991 in that **(..SPECIFY THE FAILURE(S)..)

english.notes:
This CJS Code and Standard offence Wordings is now OBSOLETE. Revoked by the Water Resources (Control of Pollution) (Silage, Slurry and Agricultural Fuel Oil) (England) Regulations 2010. S.I. 2010/639 refers

(i) Regulation 5(1) of the Control of Pollution (Silage, Slurry and Agricultural Fuel Oil) Regulations 1991 provide that fuel oil on a farm must be stored:-
(a) in a fuel storage tank within a storage area in relation to which the requirements of Schedule 3 are satisfied;
(b) in drums within such a storage area;
(c) temporarily in a tanker used for transporting fuel oil on roads or about the farm;
(d) in a fuel storage tank which is an exempt structure by virtue of regulation 6 below; or
(e) in an underground fuel storage tank.
(ii) Regulation 5(2) provides that (i) above shall not apply if the total quantity of fuel stored on the farm does not exceed 1500 litres.
(iii) Schedule 3 to the regulations set out the requirements for fuel oil storage areas.
